correctness.rationale: Domination in \(B_n\) is exactly the condition of meeting both cliques. The induced-isolate condition is equivalent to having a singleton clique-side whose unique vertex is either not the bridge endpoint or is the bridge endpoint while the opposite bridge endpoint is absent. The resulting disjoint case partition gives the displayed bivariate enumerator. Minimality forces one selected vertex on each side, with only the bridge pair excluded. The finite verifier exhaustively checks all subsets for \(2\le n\le7\), including every bivariate coefficient and all minimal sets.

value.rationale: The isolated-domination polynomial is an established refinement designed to count all feasible sets, and barbells already have a published scalar isolate-domination theorem. The exact side-by-side classification therefore fills a natural enumerative gap rather than selecting an arbitrary parameter slice. The result also separates two natural scales: isolate dominating sets exist up to size \(n+1\), while every minimal isolate dominating set has size \(2\), forcing \(\Gamma_0(B_n)=2\).
